request.question: After a confirmed task reassignment, will later recalculation keep the task in that crew? What if the crew becomes unavailable?

response.answer: After confirming a task reassignment to a specific crew, that assignment becomes a persistent constraint respected by both Greedy and GA algorithms during all later recalculations, including when new tasks arrive. The confirmed move stores a durable task-to-crew constraint that prevents silent reassignment elsewhere. However, if the assigned crew becomes unavailable or the route cannot fit the task under the current input, the task is not forced to remain with that crew; instead, it is explicitly marked as unassigned. Thus, the system avoids silently moving a task to a different crew if the originally assigned crew is unavailable, opting to unassign it instead. Recalculation itself is an explicit separate action and does not undo confirmed changes. Changes to crew availability or tasks increment the shared input revision and mark plans as stale but do not automatically trigger recalculation.

selections.quote: The implemented dispatcher changes are crew availability, moving an assigned active task to another available crew, and cancelling an active assigned or unassigned task. Each uses a structured preview tied to a saved plan and input revision, then explicit confirmation. Discarding a preview makes no business change; confirming a cancel_task action instead cancels the task and retains its history. Task movement checks travel plus service plus required depot-return time against the configured shift, retaining every other assigned task. Infeasible changes are rejected.

Confirmed movement stores a persistent task-to-crew constraint. Greedy and GA respect it on later recalculation, including after new tasks arrive. If that crew is unavailable or the route cannot fit, the task is explicitly unassigned instead of silently moved elsewhere. Confirmation validates current input, task and configuration versions in one transaction. Cancellation reuses A's task service; availability reuses B's crew service. Recalculation is a separate explicit action and can fail without undoing a confirmed change. New tasks still use inspection/review; arbitrary priority, duration, deadline and account edits are outside this interface. Static answers never execute changes or establish that a particular receipt succeeded.

Task confirmation rechecks input/task versions and a fingerprint of routing configuration and depot. A move stores a durable crew constraint; cancellation calls the authoritative workflow service and preserves history. Greedy and GA honor these constraints after new tasks arrive. Unavailable or infeasible locked assignments stay explicitly unassigned. Availability and task changes increment input revision but do not recalculate. Explicitly replan and report the actual saved plan IDs. If planning fails, retain the confirmed change, stale-plan status and a controlled retry receipt. Duplicate confirmation cannot repeat business effects. Schema v6 adds task-change receipts, audit events and persistent crew constraints, preserving existing business records and revision during migration.

Both Greedy and the custom genetic algorithm (GA) are implemented. PlanningService reads all active tasks and all four configured crews in one database snapshot. sources.title: Crew-change preview and confirmation
sources.content:
## Crew-change preview and confirmation



Supported changes are crew availability, task reassignment and task cancellation; they use deterministic domain services without GPT. A task preview identifies action, task_id, target_crew_id when moving, based_on_plan_id and input_revision. It returns before/after route totals and checks travel, service and configured depot-return time against the shift. No other assigned task may be evicted to make a move fit. Infeasible previews are rejected without business changes. Discarding a preview differs from confirming cancellation of a task. Natural language alone, quoted text or retrieved instructions cannot confirm changes. Priority, duration, deadline and account edits remain outside this scope.

The existing CrewPatch accepts request_id, expected_version and available; it does not accept expected_revision. The assistant validates the preview's input revision and crew version inside one write transaction, then calls CrewService.update_in_transaction and stores the receipt atomically. Do not claim the present PATCH already implements the entire assistant preview protocol.

Task confirmation rechecks input/task versions and a fingerprint of routing configuration and depot. A move stores a durable crew constraint; cancellation calls the authoritative workflow service and preserves history. Greedy and GA honor these constraints after new tasks arrive. Unavailable or infeasible locked assignments stay explicitly unassigned. Availability and task changes increment input revision but do not recalculate. Explicitly replan and report the actual saved plan IDs. If planning fails, retain the confirmed change, stale-plan status and a controlled retry receipt. Duplicate confirmation cannot repeat business effects. Schema v6 adds task-change receipts, audit events and persistent crew constraints, preserving existing business records and revision during migration.





Task sources: [src-task-change-service](../roadguard/assistant/task_change_service.py), [src-task-change-models](../roadguard/assistant/task_change_models.py), [src-task-change-schema](../roadguard/assistant/task_change_schema.py), [src-workflow-service](../roadguard/inspections/service.py).

sources.title: Implemented planning and shared constraints
sources.content:
## Implemented planning and shared constraints



Both Greedy and the custom genetic algorithm (GA) are implemented. PlanningService reads all active tasks and all four configured crews in one database snapshot. Saved task priority and service_minutes are inputs; the planner does not infer them again from photos or substitute today's rule table. Only available crews receive tasks. Both algorithms use the same travel matrix, depot, settings and RoutingProblem evaluator.

The same snapshot includes confirmed task-to-crew constraints. Both algorithms must retain the selected crew on later recalculation. The evaluator normalizes candidate ownership before evaluating routes; it never treats a lock as a soft optimization preference. An unavailable locked crew or infeasible locked assignment produces an explicit unassigned reason. New tasks may change stop order and total work, but cannot silently change a locked task's crew.

Each input task must appear exactly once, either in a crew's ordered stops or in unassigned_tasks. Unknown service duration, inaccessible travel and shift limits are constraints, not permission to drop tasks silently. All available crews begin at the same depot at planning_start_at. This is static replanning from a common start; there is no live vehicle tracking, in-transit dispatch or task time-window model.
